Run `fn` in a single atomic DB transaction. Retries on serialization failures / deadlocks, so callers must make `fn` free of external side effects.

Rate-limit key = client IP + targeted account (for login/register). Brute force against one account stays capped, while many people behind one NAT (common on mobile networks) are not locked out by each other.
Decimal string with up to `dp` places — never a JS float.
Double-entry ledger. All balance changes go through `post`, inside the caller's transaction. Accounts are row-locked (in id order, to avoid deadlocks) before any balance is read or written.

Logarithmic Market Scoring Rule (LMSR) for binary YES/NO markets. C(qY, qN) = b · ln(e^(qY/b) + e^(qN/b)) p_YES = ∂C/∂qY = e^(qY/b) / (e^(qY/b) + e^(qN/b)) = 1 / (1 + e^((qN − qY)/b)) Pure functions on decimal.js values

Turns an LMSR state + a trade request into an exact, rounded execution plan. Rounding always favours the market's solvency (never the trader, never the house's books in a way that could break the escrow invariant): - buy
